title: A separated morphism unramified at the points of a fibre is etale locally a closed-immersion decomposition near them
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $s\in S$, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in X$ ($n\ge0$) be points with $f(x_i)=s$ such that $f$ is unramified at each $x_i$: every $x_i$ has an open neighbourhood $X_i\subseteq X$ such that $f|_{X_i}:X_i\to S$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then there are an etale morphism $g:U\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and a point $u\in U$ with $g(u)=s$, and a decomposition of the fibre product $X_U=X\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $X_U=W\amalg\coprod_{i=1}^n\coprod_{j=1}^{m_i}V_{i,j}$ (integers $m_i\ge0$; $W$ and the $V_{i,j}$ open subschemes of $X_U$, pairwise disjoint, covering $X_U$), such that (1) for all $i,j$ the composite $V_{i,j}\hookrightarrow X_U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}U$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose image contains $u$; (2) no point of $W$ lying over $u\in U$ maps under $\mathrm{pr}_1:X_U\to X$ to any of $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. In particular, if $f^{-1}(\{s\})=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$, then no point of $W$ lies over $u$. (Stacks Project, Tag [04HI].)

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04HI (lemma-unramified-etale-local-technical, proof at lines 1722-1749), using 02LM and 04DG

proof.text: Choose unramified open neighbourhoods $X_i$ of the listed points and replace them by their finite union $X^\circ=\bigcup_iX_i$; the restriction $X^\circ\to S$ is locally of finite type and unramified at every $x_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-fibre-point-isolated] and then [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-multiple-points] to $X^\circ\to S$. This gives an etale neighbourhood and finitely many open pieces $V_{i,j}\subseteq X^\circ\times_SU$, finite over the neighbourhood, with the required points and exclusions; their inclusions into $X\times_SU$ are open. The fact that the restriction remains unramified and that the base-changed morphism is unramified is exactly [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open] (Stacks Tags 02G6 and 02GA), applied to the defining unramified neighbourhoods and to $X^\circ\to S$.

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04HI, lines 1702-1714, using More on Morphisms Lemma 02LM

proof.text: Shrink the etale neighbourhood to an affine open and use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open], each $V_{i,j}\to U$ is still unramified after the base changes and open restrictions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-unramified-one-point-closed] to each finite unramified piece and intersect the finitely many resulting neighbourhoods. Whenever the base is shrunk from $U$ to an open $U'$, replace every piece by the actual base change $V'_{i,j}:=V_{i,j}\times_UU'$; [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] identifies $V'_{i,j}$ with the corresponding inverse-image open in $X\times_SU'$. The resulting pieces are closed immersions through the chosen point.

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04HI, lines 1711-1714, and Schemes Lemma 01JR

proof.text: The base change of X to U is separated. Each closed immersion piece into U is proper, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] makes its map to the base-changed X proper and therefore closed. Pairwise intersections are closed and have closed images in U; the exclusion clause from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-multiple-points] says those images avoid the chosen point.

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04HI, lines 1737-1745; Morphisms Lemma 01W6

proof.text: Delete the finite union of those closed images from U and again replace every V by its base change along this open, using [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. The pieces are now pairwise disjoint. Their finite union is open and closed, so its open-and-closed complement W gives the asserted decomposition and the exclusion over the chosen point.

split_report.summary: Repaired the 04HI split with self-contained TeX child statements citing all scheme, fibre, finite type, etale, finite, unramified, closed-immersion, residue-field, and purely-inseparable notions. The child sources and exact Stacks tags are 02LM, 04DG, and 02G8/02GF (with 02V5 for quasi-finiteness). The parent names the defining-node stability argument and explicitly replaces each V by its base change after shrinking U, using 01JR.
